tool_input.description: Probe behavior of random() with invalid clipped range start>end after ASCII optimization

result:
The full suite (all `*AgentTest.java` files) runs cleanly with only these same 4 failures, confirming no other test in the project is affected and these failures are isolated to the bug found.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/RandomStringUtilsAgentTest.java` with 55 test methods covering the deprecated static `random*` methods, the instance-based `next*` methods, the singleton accessors (`secure()`, `insecure()`, `secureStrong()`), boundary/error cases (negative counts, empty char sets, invalid start/end ranges, missing letters/digits in a custom char set, out-of-bounds custom char arrays, unreachable code-point ranges), and deep invariants over the full-Unicode generation path (string length matches requested count, no lone surrogates, no UNASSIGNED/PRIVATE_USE/SURROGATE code points).

4 tests fail and demonstrate a real bug in `RandomStringUtils`:

- `testNextGraphInstanceCanProduceTilde`
- `testRandomGraphStaticCanProduceTilde`
- `testNextPrintInstanceCanProduceTilde`
- `testRandomPrintStaticCanProduceTilde`

**Bug:** `nextGraph`/`randomGraph` and `nextPrint`/`randomPrint` call `next(count, 33, 126, false, false)` and `next(count, 32, 126, false, false)` respectively, where the `end` parameter is documented as *exclusive*. This makes the actual generated range `[33,125]` and `[32,125]`, silently excluding `'~'` (126) — the upper bound of the documented POSIX `[:graph:]` and `[:print:]` character classes. By contrast, `nextAscii`/`randomAscii` correctly uses `end = 127` to include up to 126. This is an off-by-one: the `end` bound for `nextGraph`/`nextPrint` should be `127`, not `126`, to match their documented character ranges.
